correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southern opening and long initial feeder
correspondence.finding: Figure 2.4 includes the southern Milligan drainage boundary and scattered prairie channels, but its 1:600,000 presentation does not establish the whole selected opening-to-middle feeder as a connected mapped line. Drainage-area inclusion alone is insufficient to assign the opening the Milligan name.

correspondence.component_scope: Intermediate bend, joins and approach through the southern Milligan corridor
correspondence.finding: Figures 4.3, 4.8 and 4.15 identify the Foam Lake/PFRA or Helgasson Community Dam setting. Figure 4.8 labels Milligan Creek and shows an existing reservoir with its local creek setting. The figure is a local irrigation example; it does not connect every stored upstream bend and join to the selected lake approach. Proposed auxiliary storage and pipework are not treated as existing river passages.

correspondence.component_scope: Foam Lake and associated inlet, marsh and outlet passage
correspondence.finding: Figure 4.15 identifies Foam Lake and the surrounding Milligan irrigation/wetland project area. Printed pages 71 and 74 explicitly discuss Foam Lake water reaching downstream Milligan Creek. This supports the receiving relation, but the generalized lake/project figures do not establish the selected inlet-through-wetland-to-outlet line continuously.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Milligan wetland corridor and Little Quill approach
correspondence.finding: The regional drainage map and southeastern project figure place the northwest-trending Milligan corridor between the Foam Lake area and Little Quill Lake. The report describes lower Milligan wetland storage and a northern bifurcation. The actual lower branch sequence is not continuously distinguished in the readable project diagram, so basin and named-corridor identity are not substituted for every selected connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Little Quill and Middle Quill/Mud Lake passage
correspondence.finding: Figure 2.4 shows the connected Quill lake setting, and the 2022 introduction describes Little Quill spilling toward Big Quill and the lakes behaving as one waterbody above the connecting level. Earlier lawful 2015 prose separately identifies Middle Quill as Mud Lake. This supplies ordinary lake-complex correspondence for the selected westward lake passage; no exact shore or internal lake centreline is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Big Quill receiving lake and actual endorheic terminal
correspondence.finding: The westward final stored parts and terminal are within the Big Quill receiving-lake setting depicted in Figure 2.4. Both reports describe Big Quill as the near-terminal waterbody of a semi-closed basin. A possible future spill toward Last Mountain Lake is outside this selected endpoint and is not appended to the finding.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northwestern opening and eastward connection
correspondence.finding: The selected northwestern opening and its first eastward feeder are absent from the CEHQ original. The path approaches a depicted north-south feeder and river junction farther east, but the missing opening-to-junction connection is not established. This is an omitted through-link, not an exact-bank or headwater-vertex requirement.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper eastward corridor and turn to the south
correspondence.finding: From the depicted upper junction, the selected eastward bends and southward turn correspond to a continuous river line. The nearby Piakuakamit/Petit Mécatina geography is separate. The supported Étamamiou corridor name is not extended back over the omitted opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper southward valley and western lateral join
correspondence.finding: The selected southward descent and its western river/lake-fed junction are depicted continuously. Minor broadenings and side waters remain unnamed; no lake name is transferred from another route.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle southeastward reach, broadened waters and lateral joins
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues through the source’s connected southeastward and southward river and broadened-water corridor. Eastern and western lateral lake-fed joins remain distinct, and the printed Rivière Étamamiou label lies along this main corridor. The generalization does not support separate names for its individual broadened or lacustrine waters.

correspondence.component_scope: Western bend and connected middle-lower waterbody passages
correspondence.finding: The original depicts the selected westward bend, subsequent southward continuation, side-water connections and return toward the lower north-south reach. The selected through-route remains distinguishable from the neighboring western chain. No reservoir, managed passage or glacial connector is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Long lower north-south reach and eastward elbow
correspondence.finding: The selected long narrow waterbody/river reach and eastward lower elbow follow continuous depicted water. The Étamamiou river label supports corridor identity, while any individual lake identity remains unassigned. Correspondence ends before the station symbol begins to conceal the route.

correspondence.component_scope: Station-obscured lower connection and actual selected coastal endpoint
correspondence.finding: Station 075601’s opaque triangle conceals a lower river section; its data box hides the final selected reach and endpoint. Visible short pieces between the annotations do not establish the concealed through-links or the endpoint’s connection to the receiving coastal water. The Saumon Québec profile identifies the river and a coastal mouth setting, but does not depict these chosen connections. The modeled sea-terminal class and distinct source endpoint are not substituted for observed geography.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern opening and first northeast-trending feeder
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and initial northeastern feeder are considered from the pinned path only. No independent source map has yet been lawfully read over this interval. Independent cartography must distinguish the initial selected feeder and its first joins; a nearby named river or basin assignment cannot establish this connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper bend and east-trending lake/river corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected path turns east through a long interior chain and reaches the lower-corridor junction. No actual source pixels establish its lakes and through-links in this pass. Lake entry/exit relationships, short connecting watercourses and all selected intermediate joins remain unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeast-trending middle and lower river
correspondence.finding: Independent CHS prose identifies Big River in the coastal region, but its geographic remit does not map the selected interior course. Readable original cartography must follow the selected northeastern route to the river mouth at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual stored northward terminal extension
correspondence.finding: The stored rendering continues materially north of the earlier source sea point. CHS describes Big River entering a bight between Seal Cove Point and Porcupine Point and separately describes Adlavik Bay farther north; this is contextual prose only. The complete selected northward extension and actual endpoint remain unmatched to a depicted river or marine passage. The source mouth is not substituted for the stored endpoint.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern opening and northward approach in the Conhelo sector
correspondence.finding: The regional thesis map includes this opening sector, but does not depict the selected initial channel or its first join. No source-supported headwater name is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Easterly western turns toward Eduardo Castex
correspondence.finding: The thesis supplies terrain, scattered-lagoon and regional runoff context. It does not establish the selected west-to-east channel, intervening joins or individual depression passages.

correspondence.component_scope: Eduardo Castex approach and selected lagoon-sector passage at Monte Nievas
correspondence.finding: Figure 50 and the accompanying prose identify the Eduardo Castex–Monte Nievas regional hydrological system and lagoons receiving runoff from the west. The selected entry, passage and eastward continuation are not traced by this thematic map; the regional label is not assigned to the river.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward middle interval beyond Monte Nievas, including the southward and northward turns
correspondence.finding: This interval extends beyond the detailed eastern frame of the thesis map. The congress publication depicts a planned canal network farther east, but does not establish the intervening selected links or all lagoon entries and exits.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeasterly approach and bend into the eastern southward corridor
correspondence.finding: The congress engineering overview supplies the setting of the proposed main and secondary canals. It does not establish that this selected bend is the depicted canal or a connected natural channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward eastern interval and transition toward the mapped reservoir-planning area
correspondence.finding: Figures 6 and 7 distinguish the northern reservoir footprint within the Obra de los Daneses scheme. Geographic proximity does not establish the selected approach, reservoir entry or north-to-central connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Final southward and southeasterly turns and actual inland endpoint
correspondence.finding: Comparison with Figure 8 places the selected final interval and endpoint in the mapped central-cuenco planning footprint west of Quemú Quemú. That proposed reservoir/expropriation map identifies the terminal setting but does not independently trace the selected incoming channel or establish a natural river name. No extension beyond the actual endpoint is assigned.
